open_questions: Mutual recognition state list discrepancy: DBPR's licensure-information page listed Illinois among the 9 mutual-recognition states, while the dedicated Mutual Recognition States page and the licensure FAQ (a_id/490, updated 09/10/2026) list West Virginia instead of Illinois. The newer pages (FAQ + mutual-recognition-states page) were treated as authoritative (West Virginia included, Illinois not), but the contradiction should be confirmed with DBPR.

Branch office fee conflict: Fla. Stat. s. 475.24 caps the annual branch-office registration fee at $50, while Fla. Admin. Code 61J2-1.011(7)(b) sets the branch office fee at $64. Fla. Stat. s. 475.125 authorizes the commission to set fees by rule within caps (initial application+exam not to exceed $100; initial license and renewal not to exceed $50 per year of license duration - the $64 biennial renewal equals $32/year, within cap). Whether the $64 branch-office fee is lawful despite the s. 475.24 $50 cap was not resolved.

Exam format not officially published: DBPR pages state only that the examination is given by Pearson VUE and reference the Candidate Information Booklet. The commonly cited format (100 questions, 75% to pass) and the $36.75 exam fee appear only on third-party or vendor documents, not on DBPR/myfloridalicense.com pages found in this research.

Total DBPR application charge: Fla. Admin. Code 61J2-1.011 gives component fees (application $11 + initial license $54 broker / $46.75 sales associate), but the all-in application total cited on third-party sites ($83.75) could not be confirmed on an official source; applicants may also owe an unlicensed activity fee and a Real Estate Recovery Fund fee under s. 475.125, which were not confirmed.

flsenate.gov's full-text 2024 Chapter 475 page (https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2024/Chapter475/All) timed out on repeated attempts and was abandoned per the no-retry rule; all statute citations were instead verified on current Online Sunshine (leg.state.fl.us) section pages, which opened reliably.

Fla. Stat. s. 475.5015 was opened via the 1998 archived Online Sunshine URL; the provision's 5-year retention language is identical in substance to the current (2024) chapter text, but a current-year section URL was not located.

Rule 61J2-14.014 (interest-bearing escrow accounts) and Rule 61J2-14.010(2) (monthly reconciliation / commingling cushions) rule texts were not individually opened on flrules.org; the reconciliation duty and cushion amounts are corroborated by the official FREC Broker Course Syllabus and DBPR escrow FAQs, and 61J2-14.014(1)-(2) are described in the official 61J2-24.002 citation authority document (not opened).

Brokerage-entity registration application process and form number: beyond Fla. Stat. s. 475.15 and the $72 fee in Rule 61J2-1.011(7)(a), the specific DBPR application form and step-by-step entity registration checklist were not located in this research.

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a natural person applies for licensure as a Florida real estate sales associate (or broker).
requirements.notes: Applicant must be at least 18 years of age, hold a high school diploma or its equivalent, be honest, truthful, trustworthy, and of good character with a good reputation for fair dealing, and be competent and qualified to make real estate transactions with safety to investors and those with whom a relationship of trust and confidence is undertaken. DBPR's application checklist also requires a U.S. Social Security number to apply.
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Sales associate license: minimum personal qualifications

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When an individual applies for an initial Florida real estate sales associate license.
requirements.notes: Applicant must satisfactorily complete the commission-prescribed 63-classroom-hour pre-license course for sales associates. Per DBPR's published checklist text, the course is not required before submitting the license application and exam approval may precede course completion.
requirements.timeline: Course completion valid for 2 years (per DBPR checklist text; not independently verified by URL).
requirements.title: Sales associate license: 63-hour pre-license education course

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When an applicant for a sales associate or broker license sits for the Florida license examination.
requirements.fees: Exam fee paid separately to the exam vendor; amount unverified (see FL_DRAFT_PRE_0036).
requirements.notes: A person is entitled to take the license examination if she or he submits the appropriate signed/electronically authenticated application, digital fingerprint data, and fee. At the time of examination the applicant must submit the education completion certificate (issued by the accredited college/university/community college/registered real estate school, which must also notify the commission of the applicant's completion), the examination admissions authorization letter, and proof of identification. DBPR's published checklist text states the examination is given by Pearson VUE (checklist page not URL-verified in this session).
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Sales associate and broker license: state examination

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When any individual applies for a Florida real estate license (sales associate or broker).
requirements.fees: Fingerprint processing fee paid directly to the vendor; amount unverified.
requirements.notes: Digital fingerprints must be submitted with the application; they are forwarded to the Division of Criminal Justice Information Systems within FDLE and to the FBI for criminal history processing, and results are sent to the department to determine whether the applicant is statutorily qualified for examination. DBPR FAQ text (not URL-verified in this session) states fingerprints are taken electronically via FDLE LiveScan immediately after applying, using ORI number FL920010Z, and results may take up to 5 days.
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: License applicants: electronic fingerprinting and background check

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When an individual applies for an initial Florida real estate broker license.
requirements.notes: Applicant must satisfactorily complete the commission-prescribed 72-classroom-hour pre-license course for brokers.
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Broker license: 72-hour pre-license education course

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When an individual applies for a Florida real estate broker license (upgrade from sales associate or new broker applicant).
requirements.notes: Applicant must satisfy one of three experience paths: (1) held an active sales associate license for at least 24 months during the preceding 5 years under one or more Florida brokers or one or more brokers licensed in any other state, territory, or jurisdiction of the United States or any foreign jurisdiction; (2) held a sales associate license for at least 24 months during the preceding 5 years while employed by a governmental agency in this state performing real estate licensee duties; or (3) held an active broker license for at least 24 months during the preceding 5 years in any other state, territory, or jurisdiction of the United States or any foreign jurisdiction. Out-of-state experience requires a certification of license history.
requirements.timeline: 24 months of active licensure within the 5 years immediately preceding application.
requirements.title: Broker license: 24 months of active experience in the preceding 5 years

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a newly licensed sales associate holds a license and approaches the first renewal.
requirements.notes: Sales associates must satisfactorily complete at least 45 classroom hours of commission-prescribed post-licensing education courses before the first renewal; if not completed, the license becomes null and void and the individual must requalify (retake the pre-license course and examination). No 14-hour continuing education is required before the first renewal.
requirements.timeline: Must be completed before the first renewal of the license.
requirements.title: Sales associate: 45-hour post-licensing education before first renewal

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a newly licensed broker holds a license and approaches the first renewal.
requirements.notes: Brokers must satisfactorily complete at least 60 classroom hours of commission-prescribed post-licensing education courses before the first renewal; if not completed, the license becomes null and void. A 6-month hardship extension may be available. No 14-hour continuing education is required before the first renewal.
requirements.timeline: Must be completed before the first renewal of the license.
requirements.title: Broker: 60-hour post-licensing education before first renewal

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When an applicant holds a 4-year degree in real estate from an accredited institution and applies for licensure.
requirements.notes: A person who holds a 4-year degree in real estate from an accredited institution of higher education is exempt from the pre-license and post-license education requirements.
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Four-year real estate degree: exemption from pre- and post-licensing education

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When an attorney in good standing with the Florida Bar applies for a Florida real estate license.
requirements.citation: DBPR Real Estate licensure FAQ (a_id/707); also reflected in DBPR RE-1 application instructions
requirements.notes: Per DBPR-published FAQ text and RE-1 application instructions (reproduced on a third-party site; not URL-verified on a DBPR domain in this session), attorneys in good standing with the Florida Bar are exempt from the 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and from the 14-hour continuing education requirement, but must still complete the 45-hour post-licensing course. For broker licensure, attorneys must complete the 72-hour broker pre-license course and the 60-hour broker post-licensing course.
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Florida Bar attorneys: partial exemption from real estate education requirements

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker, broker associate, or sales associate holds an active Florida real estate license and the license period ends.
requirements.fees: Renewal fee: broker $72.00 / sales associate $64.00 per biennium (see FL_DRAFT_PRE_0014).
requirements.notes: The department renews an active license upon receipt of the renewal application and fee. Sixty days prior to the end of the license period and automatic reversion of a license to inactive status, the department must mail a notice of renewal and possible reversion to the licensee's last known address.
requirements.timeline: Each biennium of a license period; department must mail renewal notice 60 days before the end of the license period.
requirements.title: License renewal: biennial renewal on application and fee

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker, broker associate, or sales associate renews an active Florida real estate license.
requirements.fees: Course fees charged by providers; unverified.
requirements.notes: The renewal application for an active license must include proof satisfactory to the commission that the licensee completed at least 14 classroom hours of 50 minutes each of a continuing education course during each biennium. The commission may accept approved distance learning courses and substitute education courses adequate to educate licensees.
requirements.timeline: At least 14 classroom hours (50 minutes each) completed during each biennium of a license period, before renewal.
requirements.title: Continuing education: 14 classroom hours each biennium

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a licensee wants to substitute attendance at a commission meeting for part of the continuing education requirement.
requirements.notes: The commission may accept attendance at one legal agenda session of the commission as a substitute for 3 classroom hours, one time per renewal cycle. No credit for attending as a party to a disciplinary action.
requirements.timeline: One time per renewal cycle; licensee must notify the division at least 7 days in advance of intent to attend.
requirements.title: Continuing education: legal agenda session substitute for 3 hours

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When applying for, obtaining, or renewing a Florida real estate license or registering a brokerage entity or branch office.
requirements.fees: Application fee: broker $11.00, sales associate $11.00. Initial licensure fee: broker $54.00, sales associate $46.75. Biennial renewal fee: broker $72.00, sales associate $64.00. Entity registration (corp/partnership/LLC/LLP): $72.00 initial and biennial renewal. Branch office: $64.00. Late fee: $25.00.
requirements.notes: All amounts are the current rule amounts as published. Note an apparent tension: Fla. Stat. s. 475.24 caps the branch office registration fee at $50, while the rule sets it at $64 (see open questions). Applicants for initial licensure and renewal may also owe an unlicensed activity fee and a Real Estate Recovery Fund fee under s. 475.125 (not confirmed in this session).
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: DBPR Division of Real Estate license fees

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a Florida real estate license is not renewed at the end of the license period.
requirements.notes: Any license not renewed at the end of the license period automatically reverts to involuntarily inactive status and may subsequently be renewed only if the licensee meets the qualifications in s. 475.183.
requirements.timeline: Automatic reversion at the end of the license period; 60-day mailed notice before reversion (s. 475.182(4)).
requirements.title: Unrenewed license reverts to involuntarily inactive status

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a Florida real estate licensee holds or seeks to reactivate a voluntarily or involuntarily inactive license.
requirements.fees: Late renewal fee not to exceed $100 (s. 475.183(2)(b)); current renewal fee collected for each renewal period the license was involuntarily inactive.
requirements.notes: A voluntarily inactive license may be renewed under s. 475.182; commission rules may require up to 12 classroom hours of CE per year the license was inactive. A renewing voluntarily inactive licensee may elect to remain voluntarily inactive.
requirements.timeline: Involuntarily inactive for 12 months or less: reactivate with 14 hours of commission-prescribed CE. More than 12 but fewer than 24 months: 28 hours of commission-prescribed education. More than 2 years: license automatically expires, becomes null and void; department gives 90 days' notice before expiration.
requirements.title: Inactive status: voluntary and involuntary renewal/reactivation rules

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a partnership, limited liability partnership, limited liability company, or corporation acts as a real estate broker in Florida.
requirements.fees: Entity registration $72.00 initial and biennial renewal (see FL_DRAFT_PRE_0018).
requirements.notes: Each partnership, LLP, LLC, or corporation acting as a broker must register with the commission and renew the licenses or registrations of its members, officers, and directors for each license period. If the license or registration of at least one active broker member is not in force, the firm's registration is canceled automatically during that period. For a limited partnership, only the general partners must be licensed brokers or registered brokerage corporations. The commission must adopt rules allowing temporary emergency registration of a broker if a sole broker of a brokerage dies or is unexpectedly unable to remain a broker.
requirements.timeline: Registration renewed for each license period; registration cancels automatically while no active broker member's license/registration is in force.
requirements.title: Brokerage firm registration: partnership, LLP, LLC, or corporation acting as broker must register

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a corporation, partnership, LLC, or LLP registers or renews registration as a brokerage entity.
requirements.notes: Rule 61J2-1.011(1) also provides that every person, partnership, LLP, corporation, or LLC deemed a licensee under Chapter 475, F.S., must register with the Florida Real Estate Commission and secure a license for each license period.
requirements.timeline: Biennial renewal.
requirements.title: Brokerage firm registration fee

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a licensee conducts real estate business at a location other than the principal office, in the same or a different municipality or county.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 475.24; Fla. Admin. Code 61J2-1.011(7)(b)
requirements.fees: Fla. Stat. s. 475.24 caps the annual branch office registration fee at $50; Fla. Admin. Code 61J2-1.011(7)(b) sets the branch office fee at $64.00 (apparent discrepancy; see open questions).
requirements.notes: Each other place of business must be registered as a branch office. A branch office must also be maintained and registered whenever, in the commission's judgment, the business conducted at a place other than the principal office is of such a nature that the public interest requires registration. Any office is deemed a branch office if a broker's name or advertising is displayed so as to reasonably lead the public to believe the office is owned or operated by that broker. The second citation URL (fee rule) is http://flrules.elaws.us/fac/61j2-1.011/.
requirements.timeline: Annual registration under the statute; biennial fee schedule under the rule.
requirements.title: Branch offices: registration required for each additional place of business

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When an individual holds an active Florida broker license.
requirements.notes: Each active broker must maintain an office consisting of at least one enclosed room in a building of stationary construction, and must maintain a sign on or about the entrance of the principal office and each branch office that may be easily observed and read by any person about to enter. Each sign must contain the broker's name (plus trade name, if any); for a partnership or corporation, the sign must contain the firm/corporation or trade name plus the name of at least one of the brokers. At a minimum the words 'licensed real estate broker' or 'lic. real estate broker' must appear on office entrance signs.
requirements.timeline: Ongoing while the broker license is active.
requirements.title: Broker must maintain an office with entrance sign

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker, or a sales associate acting as agent of the registered employer, receives money, funds, deposits, checks, or drafts entrusted to them in a real estate transaction.
requirements.notes: Failure to place, as soon after receipt as is practicably possible, any money, fund, deposit, check, or draft entrusted to the licensee (other than a bona fide check payable to a principal) in escrow with a title company, banking institution, credit union, or savings and loan association located in Florida, or to place the same in the broker's trust or escrow account, is a violation. A sales associate must immediately place with her or his registered employer any money, fund, deposit, check, or draft entrusted to her or him by any person dealing with her or him as agent of the registered employer. Violation is grounds for denial, probation, suspension (up to 10 years), revocation, administrative fine up to $5,000 per count, and/or reprimand under s. 475.25(1).
requirements.timeline: Immediately - defined as no later than the end of the third business day following receipt (see FL_DRAFT_PRE_0022).
requirements.title: Escrow: broker must immediately place entrusted funds in escrow

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker establishes and maintains escrow or trust accounts for funds entrusted in real estate transactions.
requirements.notes: Escrow accounts may only be maintained at Florida banks, trust companies, title companies with trust powers, credit unions, or savings and loan associations. No personal funds of any licensee may be deposited or intermingled with escrow funds except as provided in Rule 61J2-14.010(2) (the $5,000 property-management / $1,000 sales cushions; see FL_DRAFT_PRE_0025).
requirements.timeline: 'Immediately' means placement no later than the end of the third business day following receipt; Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays are not business days.
requirements.title: Escrow accounts: Florida depositories only, no commingling, 'immediately' defined

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a sales associate receives any deposit (as defined in Rule 61J2-14.008) in a real estate transaction.
requirements.notes: Rule text quoted verbatim in the official DOAH Recommended Order in DBPR Division of Real Estate vs. Gregory John Owen (Case No. 09-002995PL): every sales associate who receives any deposit must deliver it to the broker or employer no later than the end of the next business day following receipt. Receipt by a sales associate or any other representative of the brokerage firm constitutes receipt by the broker for purposes of Rule 61J2-14.008(1)(d). Violation is also a violation of s. 475.25(1)(e) (violating a lawful rule).
requirements.timeline: No later than the end of the next business day following receipt; Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays are not business days.
requirements.title: Escrow: sales associate must deliver deposits to broker by end of next business day

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker maintains escrow or trust accounts holding deposits, funds, money, checks, drafts, personal property, or items of value received in real estate transactions.
requirements.notes: Rule text quoted in the official DOAH Recommended Order in Case No. 09-002995PL: every broker who receives from sales associates, principals, prospects, or others any deposit, fund, money, check, draft, personal property, or item of value must immediately place it in an insured escrow or trust account at a bank, savings and loan association, trust company, credit union, or title company having trust powers. The broker must be a signatory on all escrow accounts (if the brokerage entity has more than one broker licensee, one broker licensee may be designated as the signatory). If the deposit is in securities intended to be converted into cash, conversion must be made at the earliest practical time and proceeds immediately deposited.
requirements.timeline: Immediate placement upon receipt.
requirements.title: Escrow accounts: broker must be a signatory; accounts must be insured

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker holds escrow funds and keeps a small amount of personal or brokerage funds in the account to maintain it.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 475.25(1)(k); Rule 61J2-14.010(2) (cited in rule and FREC syllabus)
requirements.notes: The statute and rule permit keeping up to $5,000 of personal or brokerage funds in the broker's rental distribution (property management) escrow account and up to $1,000 of personal or brokerage funds in the broker's sales escrow account to maintain the account. DBPR's published escrow FAQ confirms these amounts. This is the sole permitted commingling; anything more is a violation of s. 475.25(1)(k).
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Escrow: limited commingling cushion ($5,000 property management / $1,000 sales)

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker maintains escrow or trust accounts (subject to DBPR office inspection and escrow account audit).
requirements.citation: FREC Broker Course Syllabus (FREC Course II), Session 4: Escrow Management, II.B (incorporated by reference on flrules.org)
requirements.notes: The official FREC syllabus requires the broker to prepare a monthly reconciliation statement and to review, sign, and date the monthly statement reconciliation (including calculating the broker's trust liability and the reconciled bank balance). DBPR office inspections include an escrow account audit covering monthly reconciliation statements, bank statements and canceled checks, checkbooks/deposit books, ledgers, pending sale contracts, voided contracts with escrow funds held, earnest money disputes, and property management contracts.
requirements.timeline: Monthly.
requirements.title: Escrow: monthly reconciliation statement prepared, reviewed, signed, and dated by broker

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker receives a deposit in a real estate transaction.
requirements.notes: Rule text quoted in the official DOAH Recommended Order in DBPR Division of Real Estate vs. Guirlande Mardy (Case No. 13-0011PL): a broker who receives a deposit must preserve and make available to the DBPR (or its authorized representative) all deposit slips and statements of account rendered by the depository, together with all agreements between the parties to the transaction; must keep an accurate account of each deposit transaction and each separate bank account wherein funds were deposited; and all such books and accounts are subject to inspection by DBPR or its authorized representatives at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
requirements.timeline: Ongoing; records subject to DBPR inspection at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
requirements.title: Escrow records: preserve deposit slips, statements, agreements; keep accurate accounts; open to DBPR inspection

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker conducts a real estate brokerage business (whether or not funds are entrusted).
requirements.notes: Each broker must keep and make available to the department such books, accounts, and records as will enable the department to determine compliance with Chapter 475, and must preserve at least one legible copy of all books, accounts, and records pertaining to the brokerage business for the periods above. If any record was the subject of or served as evidence for litigation, it must be retained at least 2 years after conclusion of the civil action or appellate proceeding, whichever is later, but in no case less than the 5 years above. Disclosure documents required under ss. 475.2755, 475.276, and 475.278 must be retained by the licensee in all transactions resulting in a written contract to purchase and sell real property. Note: the opened page is the 1998 archived version; the 2024 chapter text is identical in substance for this provision (see open questions).
requirements.timeline: At least 5 years from the date of receipt of any money, fund, deposit, check, or draft entrusted to the broker; if no funds are entrusted, at least 5 years from the date of execution by any party of any listing agreement, offer to purchase, rental property management agreement, rental or lease agreement, or other written or verbal agreement engaging the broker's services.
requirements.title: Brokerage business records: retain for at least 5 years

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a deposit in a sales transaction is placed or to be placed with a title company or an attorney rather than in the broker's escrow account.
requirements.notes: The licensee who prepared or presented the sales contract must indicate on the contract the name, address, and telephone number of the title company or attorney. The verification-request requirement does not apply if the deposit is held by a title company or attorney nominated in writing by the seller or the seller's agent.
requirements.timeline: Broker must make written request for verification within 10 business days after each deposit is due under the sales contract; broker must provide the seller's broker (or the seller directly, if unrepresented) with a copy of the written verification, or written notice that no verification was received, within 10 business days of the date the request was made.
requirements.title: Escrow: deposits placed with a title company or attorney - contract disclosure and verification

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a licensee in good faith entertains doubt as to who is entitled to escrowed property, or conflicting demands are made for escrowed property the licensee still maintains in escrow or trust.
requirements.notes: Failure to account for or deliver entrusted property (including escrowed property) is a violation, but when good-faith doubt or conflicting demands exist, the licensee must promptly notify the commission and promptly pursue one of four escape procedures: (1) request an Escrow Disbursement Order (EDO) from FREC; (2) arbitration with the written consent of all parties; (3) interpleader or other court action; or (4) mediation completed within 90 days. Per DBPR's escrow FAQ, the broker should disburse funds promptly upon receiving the Final Order on an EDO (no fixed number of days in the rule). Exemptions to the notification/settlement requirements exist for condominium rescission periods and financing-contingency clauses (per FREC syllabus).
requirements.timeline: Promptly notify the commission; DBPR's published escrow FAQ states notification must be made within 15 working days to the Division of Real Estate - Escrow Section, 400 West Robinson Street, Suite N801, Orlando, Florida. If mediation is chosen, it must be completed within 90 days.
requirements.title: Escrow disputes: notify FREC of conflicting demands or good-faith doubt and pursue a settlement procedure

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker wants escrowed deposits to earn interest.
requirements.citation: DBPR Division of Real Estate - Real Estate Escrow FAQ (interest-bearing escrow account item)
requirements.notes: Per DBPR's published escrow FAQ, all parties should execute a written agreement to have interest accrue on the deposit and specify to whose benefit the interest is accruing; the account must be insured. The FREC syllabus and citation authority (Rule 61J2-24.002) reference Rule 61J2-14.014(1)-(2): written permission of all interested parties is required before placing trust funds in an interest-bearing escrow account, and interest must stop accruing prior to disbursement (rule text not individually opened in this session).
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Escrow: interest-bearing escrow accounts require written agreement of all parties

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker is not holding any entrusted funds in connection with real estate transactions.
requirements.citation: DBPR Division of Real Estate - Real Estate Escrow FAQ (a_id/1857, citing s. 475.25(1)(d), F.S.)
requirements.notes: Per DBPR's published escrow FAQ, a broker is not required to maintain an escrow account if the broker is not holding any funds that must be escrowed.
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: Escrow: broker not required to maintain an escrow account if not holding funds

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a broker employs or supervises sales associates or broker associates and maintains trust/escrow accounts.
requirements.notes: It is a separate violation for a broker to fail to direct, control, or manage a broker associate or sales associate employed by the broker, and to fail to review the trust accounting procedures of the brokerage (in addition to the escrow duties above).
requirements.timeline: Ongoing.
requirements.title: Broker supervision: direct, control, and manage associates; review trust accounting procedures

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a licensee, registrant, permittee, or applicant engages in misconduct under Chapter 475.
requirements.fees: Administrative fine up to $5,000 per count or separate offense (s. 475.25(1)).
requirements.notes: The commission may deny, place on probation, suspend (up to 10 years), revoke, fine (up to $5,000 per count), and/or reprimand a licensee who: commits fraud, misrepresentation, concealment, false promises, dishonest dealing, culpable negligence, or breach of trust (b); fails to account for or deliver entrusted property (d)1.; shares commissions with an unlicensed person (h); or makes false statements or records (l).
requirements.timeline: Suspension may not exceed 10 years.
requirements.title: Discipline: grounds for denial, suspension, revocation, or fine of a real estate license

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission
requirements.applies_when: When a nonresident holds an active real estate license (sales associate or broker) in one of the 9 mutual-recognition states and applies for the equivalent Florida license.

forms.name: Sales Associate Initial Application - Mutual Recognition Application for Non-FL Residents Only (RE 1)

requirements.notes: Florida has mutual recognition with 9 states: Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, Nebraska, Rhode Island, and West Virginia (see open questions re: Illinois). Qualifying brokers and sales associates are exempt from Florida pre-license education but must pass the 40-question Florida laws section of the state exam (at least 30 correct required, per the mutual recognition page) and remain subject to Florida post-licensing and continuing education requirements.
requirements.timeline: Must not be a Florida resident at time of application; must hold an active license in the mutual-recognition state.
requirements.title: Mutual recognition: out-of-state licensees from 9 states may license without pre-license education

requirements.agency: DBPR Division of Real Estate / Florida Real Estate Commission (exam administered by Pearson VUE)
requirements.applies_when: When an applicant schedules the Florida real estate license examination.
requirements.citation: Pearson VUE Real Estate and Appraiser Fact Sheet (third-party exam vendor document)
requirements.notes: The Pearson VUE fact sheet lists a $36.75 examination fee for Real Estate Salesperson and Real Estate Broker (3.5 hours) and $15.75 for Real Estate Law (1.5 hours). DBPR's own published pages do not state the exam fee; the DBPR checklist directs applicants to the Candidate Information Booklet and to pay the fee provided in the application. Not confirmed on an official Florida government source.
requirements.timeline: unverified
requirements.title: License examination fee paid to exam vendor
